newsitem.title: UK: London silver tumbles, but gold little affected.
newsitem.headline: London silver tumbles, but gold little affected.

text.p: Silver prices fell sharply on a bout of selling on Monday afternoon, applying pressure to the other precious metals.
But gold sustained minimal damage from its stable mate's losses, as the bullion market was content to hold to a narrow price range ahead of the New Year holiday, dealers added.
Bullion was fixed slightly easier at $369.25 an ounce, against $369.60 in the morning and $369.40 on Friday afternoon.
"Gold has barely had any movement at all and seems unimpressed by silver's gyrations," a London-based dealer said.
"The market is a bit thin and nervous and doesn't want to get involved in anything ahead of the year-end," he added.

Several dealers said they expected gold prices to remain in a tight range around $368-$370 this week, although gold was poised to break out soon to judge from price charts and sour market sentiment that favour the downside, they added.
But silver surprised some market makers by shedding about 10 cents an ounce in a flurry of New York-led trade and fund selling, after a quiet start to the day.
Prices settled near the $4.80 support level, which was appearing to hold for the time being. A confirmed breach of that level was seen targeting $4.75 and then $4.70.
"Silver's had a bit of a smash-up," a dealer said, adding that the sharp movement was unexpected.
"There was some options-related trade selling and probably some small (investment) funds sold into the weakness," he said.
The other white metals also eased in sympathy with silver, although they remained nestled comfortably within recent prices ranges amid quiet trading conditions.
"The whites are all looking weaker, but silver's the only real mover," a dealer said.
Platinum was indicated at $369.00/$370.00, little changed from Friday's closing levels but down $1.50 against early European levels.
It was bid as low as $367 an ounce during silver's descent, before bouncing up in thin volumes.
Palladium initially eased to $116.00 before creeping back up to the opening level of $116.50/$117.50 an ounce.
